negative_results.approach: Exact Gaussian closure (full bivariate-normal ReLU moments instead of ARC's truncated expansion)
negative_results.tried: 256-wide He-ReLU dev nets, sigma 0.001, nMSE at depth 8, 16, 32 against kprop K=2
negative_results.outcome: 1.63e-4 vs 1.63e-4 at depth 8; 7.6e-4 vs 6.2e-4 at depth 32: no gain
negative_results.why_failed: not explained beyond 'no gain' (closure errors at depth are 69-84% orthogonal to the mean direction)
negative_results.rules_out: This closure as an improvement on K=2. Does not exclude other closures.

negative_results.approach: C1 recursive moment control (Gaussian closure with non-Gaussian corrections from particles of the true net)
negative_results.tried: depths 8 and 32; 2^10-2^14 iid particles; Kerdock particles; dev net 100
negative_results.outcome: layer 1 is 30x below MC, but 2-3x over MC on the same particles at depth 8 (below the Kerdock sampler once its extra cost is counted), no gain at depth 32, none on Kerdock particles
negative_results.why_failed: correction noise and covariance bias accumulate with depth
negative_results.rules_out: This control scheme at depth. Killed before PREREG, so not a registered test.

negative_results.approach: C2 homogeneous scale-mixture closure (carry the norm mode as an exact scale)
negative_results.tried: dev nets, depth 32, sigma 0.001
negative_results.outcome: 9% better than our Gaussian closure but 11% worse than K=2 at depth 32
negative_results.why_failed: closure errors at depth are 69-84% orthogonal to the mean direction, so fixing the scale does not fix them
negative_results.rules_out: Scale as the main source of closure error at 256 x 32.
negative_results.evidence_label: exploratory (killed by the >= 2x rule, seen before PREREG)

negative_results.approach: C3 mode-cumulant closure (Edgeworth readout with cumulants from the top-k covariance modes)
negative_results.tried: one-step readout with true moments at layers 16 and 31, 3 dev nets; gate >= 5x with k <= 8
negative_results.outcome: top-8 modes give 1.9-4.1x; per-neuron cumulants of the next pre-activations give 19-120x. Failed the gate; not built
negative_results.why_failed: the missing information is per-neuron and fourth-order, not in the collapse modes
negative_results.rules_out: Low-mode cumulant closures with k <= 8. Carrying per-neuron cumulants by ARC's K=4 costs about 1e14 FLOPs (a cost for that algorithm, not a lower bound).
negative_results.evidence_label: registered gate, oracle test on 3 dev nets

negative_results.approach: Neuron/copula code at depth
negative_results.tried: layer 24 replaced by empirical per-neuron marginals (2^18 paths) with Gaussian dependence, then the real layers; dev net
negative_results.outcome: nMSE 2.3e-4 at depth 32, no better than a Gaussian with the true moments (2.1e-4)
negative_results.why_failed: the depth-32 means depend on non-Gaussian dependence at intermediate layers
negative_results.rules_out: Marginals + Gaussian copula at a cut (for the replacements tested); 'not every possible description'.

negative_results.approach: Meet in the middle, sample-free side (Gaussian description up to layer m, exact network after)
negative_results.tried: Gaussian with the true mean and covariance at m = 8, 16, 24, then real layers (2^20 paths), 3 dev nets
negative_results.outcome: nMSE 8.0e-5 to 5.0e-4 at depth 32, 12-75x the Kerdock sampler's error at the Phase-1 budget
negative_results.why_failed: non-Gaussian joint structure at intermediate layers
negative_results.rules_out: Gaussian replacements at those layers; not every description.

negative_results.approach: H1 / C4: Kerdock sampler + linear control at layer m with a kprop mean
negative_results.tried: 24 evaluation nets, depth 32, sigma 0.001, measured equal budgets 5e10-3e11, factorized K=3 mean at m = 4..24
negative_results.outcome: 0.03-0.9x of the Kerdock sampler at every m (oracle with exact layer-m mean: 1.6-2.0x at m = 16, 4.1-5.5x at m = 24). Killed. Depth 8: 1.07-1.13x at three budgets, 0.34-0.95x elsewhere, below H2 everywhere
negative_results.why_failed: the bias of ARC's K3f mean at layer m turns the control into a loss; a control mean would need about 1e-6 accuracy at depth >= 16
negative_results.rules_out: Linear controls fed by ARC's closures at depth 32. Does not exclude controls with a better mid-depth description (that is ARC's open problem).

negative_results.approach: H2 hybrid at depth 32, primary noise levels
negative_results.tried: 24 evaluation nets, sigma 0.001 and 0.003, 1e9-3e11 FLOPs
negative_results.outcome: 0.84-1.06x of the Kerdock sampler; predicted gain at 1e9-5e9 not significant
negative_results.why_failed: kprop's depth-32 error (2.2e-4 for K3f at 2.06e11 FLOPs) is far above the sampler's
negative_results.rules_out: Output-level combination of kprop and a sampler at depth 32 at sigma <= 0.003.

negative_results.approach: C6 antithetic noise on the Kerdock design at sigma <= 0.03
negative_results.tried: 24 evaluation nets, sigma 0.01 and 0.03, depths 8 and 32
negative_results.why_failed: noise is under 30% of the output variance at those levels

negative_results.approach: Monte Carlo with the last noise integrated per neuron
negative_results.tried: 24 evaluation nets, sigma <= 0.01
negative_results.outcome: 1-3% worse than plain MC
negative_results.why_failed: its readout costs more than the variance it removes
negative_results.rules_out: Last-layer Rao-Blackwellisation as a gain at low noise.

negative_results.approach: Two-level sampling over depth with a sampled coarse level

question: Does the (1/eps)^Theta(n) summary-size law survive nonlinear readouts of a summary and bounded back-and-forth methods, so that it would cover ARC's actual estimators?
claim: No, as stated: the law survives only for bounded-degree readouts and as bit counts; Lipschitz / C^k readouts and real-valued two-round protocols need counts that do not grow with 1/eps, so size bounds cannot cover ARC's closures.
status_qualifier: the breaking constructions and surviving bounds are labelled PROVEN; many are by AI co-prover gpt-6-astra, checked by the lane agent (Claude Opus 5.5) and reviewed by gpt-6-astra in a fresh session; not human-checked; all asymptotic in eps at fixed architecture.
status_evidence: Summary: 'Short answer: no, as stated.'
Summary item 1: 'So the precision exponent belonged to linear readouts.'
Summary: 'All bounds are asymptotic in eps at a fixed architecture, with astronomically small constants.'
Section 5: 'A polylogarithmic state is not a loss to sampling.'
Section 5: 'It concerns ARC's closure fed exact cumulants. The full algorithm propagates estimated cumulants, and earlier errors could cancel the final step's bias.'
Section 10, L1: 'Status: not yet a precise target. Information arguments cannot give it: weights and finite moments already suffice.'
Section 2: 'All entries are PROVEN. The analytic upper bound (Addendum 2) was checked by the final review, not by the co-prover.'

corrections.what: Section 3.6 compared the formula with d = PR (224 / 112 / 45 bits at l = 4 / 8 / 16, net 4000, nMSE 0.1) with interim learned counts 230 / 104 / 34-52 and called it within 3-8% at l = 4 and 8. The later variable-rate counts on the same net are 192 / 82 / 27 (look-ahead start; 236 / 100 / 32 from the reference start), so the formula is 1.2 / 1.4 / 1.7 times the registered count (P1.7, within 2x: pass). Those later counts are themselves upper bounds (layer 16 at 10%: 24 bits with 8x steps). Layer 0, '>256' here, was resolved to 575 bits (net 4000).

The counts used in 3.6 were an interim relay for net 4000. The final table gives medians over four nets of >256 (l = 4), 135 (l = 8), 43-46 (l = 16), 25 (l = 24), 24 (l = 31), output 25; and at l = 8 and l = 24 only the linear transform code was run ('C learned' is empty there), so '104 at l = 8' is a linear-code count, not a learned one.
Small correction to the relevance lane's Corollary 1b (average the right side over the singular values), from this lane's co-prover round 2.

Finite-width '1.7-3.3x enhancement' of the cubic law was a normalisation artifact; the forward-only / two-sided separation holds averaged over futures, not for a fixed net; the hash proposition's smallest gain is 4(K-1)/K, not 'at least 4'.

'References are samples' is an upper bound, not a lower bound; the point-method rate is conjectural without the surrogate; the closure cost describes one implementation; the 'best' merge is not forward-only; 'the error stops falling, the gain peaks, the lead is closed' softened to moderate evidence for a peak and 'weakened, not closed'; Prop 7.7's sign corrected; C_V recomputed (13.481).
The hardness lane's K = 2 slopes, cited as evidence on closures, describe ARC's truncated recursion, not the exact Gaussian closure.

Martingale needs the frozen-at-death convention; profile constants came from a truncated sum (10.63, 0.058) and a wrong approximation 5.5/(l + 5.5), now 10.65, 0.060 and 8.3/(l + 9); the lower bound is a theorem for an idealised source only; the 88% agreement on old nets mostly counts censored and zero-bit cases (23 of 64 resolved); the enumeration comparison is not a necessary condition for beating sampling.

question: Does Kelvin's backward recursion (train the code at each layer to the bits of the next layer's code minus the bits the noise erases) give certified bit counts of fixed encodings from the output back to the input on small noisy nets?
claim: The target (next code's bits minus erased bits) is the right ceiling (proved), but no fixed encoding carries its own rate's worth of it and the chain drifts: Kelvin's rule keeps a median 26% of the truth at the input.
status_qualifier: registered (B1-B12: 6 hit, 6 missed; B13-B14 amended after the outcome, not registered outcomes); propositions proved by the Claude lane agent, checked by Claude main and by gpt-6-astra (r1: Props 1, 2, 6 pass, Prop 3 restricted; r2: Prop 7's induction correct); no human check; conditional on one fixed 64-cell output quantiser per net and one noise level per config; two leaks in the direct comparator disclosed and not rerun
status_evidence: Header: 'Status: FINAL v2 (scored runs complete 20:39Z; gpt-6-astra round 2 applied 21:00Z).'

Summary, short answer: 'So: certified targets to the input, yes; certified bit counts of fixed encodings to the input, no: your rule meets the registered criterion on no config; 3 of 16 config-rule pairs meet it, and on those the 95% level is often not reached, only stably approached (4.3).'
Summary, short answer: 'Everything is conditional on one fixed 64-cell output quantiser per net and one noise level per config.'

components.item: On Kelvin's question (do correctly compressed bits get scrambled between layers)
components.label: not a scrambling test; PROVEN and MEASURED loss mechanism
components.note: Codes compressed to exactly the target rate lose 22-49% of the target at the first step where the noise erases about a bit, and the loss compounds to a median 26% of the truth at the input. The stated cause is not scrambling: with Gaussian noise every next-code value is possible given any h_l, so a partition code cannot be a function of the next code (Prop 2). The arithmetic is exact for stochastic re-simulation codes (Prop 7), which were not run.

corrections.what: Reinterpretation: the shared-noise score is 'a different count'; with the future noise shared nothing is erased, so it needs at least H(c_{l+1} | xi) >= T_l bits (PROVEN). Codes trained forward on that distortion (S4 style) carry less than the chains' codes at equal rate and collapse to about 0 bits at the input layers: 'not a usable baseline at the input'.
